findings.finding: The domain is the string set {a}*, but the addition and multiplication interpretations take natural-number arguments n and m rather than strings.
findings.controlling_evidence: The intended isomorphism maps n to a^n, so the two function inputs must be a^n and a^m while the displayed outputs remain a^(n+m) and a^(nm).
findings.required_translation_handling: Use a^n and a^m as the displayed arguments and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-001 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 24-39, purported L_A structure and isomorphism claim

findings.finding: The source calls M an L_A-structure and says it is isomorphic to N but never interprets the predicate <.
findings.controlling_evidence: Interpreting a^n < a^m exactly when n<m completes the L_A-structure and makes the stated isomorphism true.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add only the length-order interpretation and an adjacent OLTEMODARI-002 disclosure.

findings.finding: After introducing x as the existential witness, the repeated proof predicate omits x and supplies only the contradiction code.
findings.controlling_evidence: The consistency formula immediately above uses the binary predicate Prf_PA(x, code(false)), and the prose calls x the Goedel number of a derivation.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore x as the first proof-predicate argument and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-003 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 152-170, characterization of a suitable successor map

findings.finding: Failure of surjectivity is said to leave an element outside the domain of s, although s is already declared on all of M.
findings.controlling_evidence: Surjectivity concerns the range; the following existential predecessor sentence likewise asserts that every nonzero point is in that range.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use range in the Telugu reasoning and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-004 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 83-98, expansion by the new constant c

findings.finding: The new constant c is evaluated as Assign(c,M), even though it exists only in the expanded structure M^c and is forgotten in M.
findings.controlling_evidence: The paragraph explicitly distinguishes the expanded model M^c from its L_A-reduct M.
findings.required_translation_handling: Evaluate c in M^c and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-005 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proof chooses the largest k with c not equal to numeral k in Gamma_0 without handling a finite subset containing no such constraint.
findings.controlling_evidence: If there is no c-constraint, any expansion of N suffices; assigning c the value 0 is a concrete witness.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add the no-constraint case before choosing k and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-006 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proposition asserts an enumerable non-standard model, but the proof uses compactness only to obtain an unrestricted model.
findings.controlling_evidence: The expanded language is countable, so Downward Lowenheim--Skolem supplies a countable elementary submodel; the parallel frozen nonstandard-arithmetic section states this step explicitly.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add the Downward Lowenheim--Skolem countability step and an adjacent OLTEMODARI-007 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 96-107, Q_5 case split for K

findings.finding: The final case split says y=b although K has domain N union {a} and contains no b.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed calculation immediately below uses y=a, which is the only non-standard case in K.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use y=a and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-008 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 154-171, Q_5 case split for L

findings.finding: The b-plus-a case ends with (b plus y)^succ even though this branch fixes the second argument as a.
findings.controlling_evidence: The operation table gives b plus a=b and the equality chain therefore ends with (b plus a)^succ.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace the stray y by a and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-009 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proposition claims every x has a predecessor, including zero, although zero is the least element and Q proves it is not a successor.
findings.controlling_evidence: The correct discrete arithmetic statement gives a unique predecessor exactly for x not equal to zero.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add the nonzero restriction and an adjacent OLTEMODARI-010 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proof switches three times from the chapter's defined model-addition notation nsplus to an unrelated opulus symbol.
findings.controlling_evidence: All preceding and following block calculations use nsplus for Assign(+,M), and the proposition concerns that same operation.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use nsplus in all three places and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-011 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 238-258, order type of non-standard blocks

findings.finding: The source says the non-standard blocks form a denumerable order without assuming the model is countable.
findings.controlling_evidence: Uncountable models may have uncountably many blocks; the next sentence itself restricts the isomorphism conclusion to enumerable models.
findings.required_translation_handling: State density and endpointlessness generally, and denumerability only for a countable model; add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-012 disclosure.

findings.finding: The ordered-pair set builder uses pairs <x,a> but constrains an unrelated variable n to the domain.
findings.controlling_evidence: The earlier definition of K in OLP-0195 correctly constrains x in Domain(K).
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace n by x in the set-builder condition and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-013 disclosure.

findings.finding: The source says N is literally the only computable PA-model, but computable transports of N along nonidentity computable permutations give distinct computable copies on domain N.
findings.controlling_evidence: Tennenbaum's theorem rules out computable non-standard PA-models; equivalently, every computable PA-model is standard, i.e. isomorphic to N.
findings.required_translation_handling: State uniqueness up to isomorphism/every computable model is standard and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-014 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 68-98, transport of K to domain N

findings.finding: The claimed bijection g(0)=a and g(n)=n+1 for n>0 omits both 0 and 1 and contradicts the transported operation formulas below it.
findings.controlling_evidence: Using g(n)=n-1 for n>0 is a bijection N to N union {a}, sends 1 to K's zero, and yields exactly the printed x+y-1 and xy-x-y+2 pullback formulas.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace n+1 by n-1 in the map and add an adjacent OLTEMODARI-015 disclosure.
